newsitem.title: USA: N.Carolina cotton plantings progress but trail avg.
newsitem.headline: N.Carolina cotton plantings progress but trail avg.

text.p: North Carolina's cotton farmers planted 30 percent of the intended acreage in one week but progress continued to lag the average pace, the agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop update.

Cotton was 65 percent planted as of Sunday, up from 35 percent the previous week but behind the average of 78 percent. The crop was rated one percent very poor, nine percent poor, 37 percent fair, 45 percent good and eight percent excellent.
Corn was 98 percent seeded, topping the five-year average of 96 percent. Conditions were nil very poor, four percent poor, 33 fair, 57 percent good and six percent excellent.
Soybeans were 21 percent seeded, just off the average of 22 percent. The crop was rated 14 percent fair, 72 percent good and 14 percent excellent.
"Some localized areas are concerned that the cooler than normal temperatures may hamper germination of the cotton and peanut crops," the report said.
Temperatures averaged eight degrees below normal for the week.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, 20 percent short, 72 percent adequate and seven percent surplus.
